summary:
## Summary

**What the change does:** Adds `lookup.go`, a single new HTTP handler `(*Store).LookupHandler` that returns accounts filtered by a caller-supplied `region` query parameter.

**What I examined:** The full diff, the whole repository (only `go.mod`, `store.go`, `lookup.go` are tracked), and searched for any other definition or caller of `LookupHandler` / `writeAccounts` to see whether a validation or auth layer exists. `store.go` contains only the `Store` type, a constructor, and a parameterized `Count` query — no sanitization helper, no middleware. Routing/authentication is not present in this repository, so reachability by an unauthenticated caller is genuinely undeterminable from here and I recorded it as `unclear`.

**Conclusion:** One finding — a textbook SQL injection: the `region` request parameter flows unchecked from `r.URL.Query().Get` into a `fmt.Sprintf`-built SQL string executed with `QueryContext`, inside a single-quoted literal the attacker can break out of. This yields read access to arbitrary rows/tables (ids, emails, and anything reachable via `UNION`). Fix is to bind the value as a query parameter.

Note: `writeAccounts` is referenced but not defined anywhere in the tracked tree, so this package does not compile as committed — worth flagging to the author, though it is not itself a security issue.

verdict.reason: 1 finding(s) at or above the high threshold with at least medium confidence (1 high).

findings.title: SQL injection via unvalidated `region` query parameter in LookupHandler
findings.evidence:
rows, err := s.db.QueryContext(r.Context(),
		fmt.Sprintf("SELECT id, email FROM accounts WHERE region = '%s'", region))
findings.description: `LookupHandler` reads the `region` value straight from the HTTP query string (`r.URL.Query().Get("region")`) and interpolates it into the SQL text with `fmt.Sprintf` before executing it via `QueryContext`. There is no escaping, quoting, allowlist, or type coercion anywhere between the source and the sink — the value is placed inside a single-quoted literal that the attacker can terminate with a `'` character. The rest of the package (store.go) shows no validation layer, and no other code in the repository wraps or sanitizes this handler.
findings.exploit_scenario: An attacker requests `GET /lookup?region=x'%20OR%20'1'%3D'1` and receives every row of `accounts` (all ids and emails) instead of one region. With `region=x' UNION SELECT id, password_hash FROM users --` they can pivot to other tables and exfiltrate credentials; on drivers/configurations that allow multiple statements the same injection point permits writes (e.g. `'; UPDATE accounts SET ...--`).
findings.recommendation: Use a bound parameter instead of string formatting: `s.db.QueryContext(r.Context(), "SELECT id, email FROM accounts WHERE region = $1", region)` (or `?` depending on the driver). If the region set is fixed, additionally validate against an allowlist before querying.

verification.reason: 2/3 verifier(s) agreed — lookup.go:11 reads `region` directly from `r.URL.Query()` and lookup.go:13-14 interpolates it into the SQL text with fmt.Sprintf inside a single-quoted literal before executing it via QueryContext, so no driver-side parameterization occurs. I searched the entire repository (only go.mod, store.go, lookup.go exist) for any validator, allowlist, escaping helper, or middleware — store.go contains only New/Count with a static query, and no such control exists anywhere; grep for LookupHandler found no wrapper or route registration either. The sink is added by this change, so exploitability depends on how the handler is mounted, but the handler is an exported method on an exported Store type in a library package clearly intended to be routed, which makes this latent-but-real rather than harmless. Searched: Searched the whole repo (3 tracked files: go.mod, store.go, lookup.go) for a validator/allowlist/escaping step or an auth wrapper: `search_code` for LookupHandler/writeAccounts found only the definition and its own call, no callers or middleware; store.go:12-15 shows the only other query and it is a static string with no sanitizing helpers. writeAccounts is not even defined in the repo, confirming the package is mid-wiring. Conclusion: no such check exists.

votes.reasoning: lookup.go:11 reads `region` directly from `r.URL.Query()` and lookup.go:13-14 interpolates it into the SQL text with fmt.Sprintf inside a single-quoted literal before executing it via QueryContext, so no driver-side parameterization occurs. I searched the entire repository (only go.mod, store.go, lookup.go exist) for any validator, allowlist, escaping helper, or middleware — store.go contains only New/Count with a static query, and no such control exists anywhere; grep for LookupHandler found no wrapper or route registration either. The sink is added by this change, so exploitability depends on how the handler is mounted, but the handler is an exported method on an exported Store type in a library package clearly intended to be routed, which makes this latent-but-real rather than harmless.

lookup.go is added wholesale by this MR and the entire flow is visible in one function: `region` comes from `r.URL.Query().Get("region")` (line 11) and is interpolated with fmt.Sprintf into a single-quoted SQL literal executed by `s.db.QueryContext` (lines 13-14), with no escaping, allowlist, regex check, or type coercion between them. I searched the whole repository (only go.mod, store.go, lookup.go exist) for any validator, middleware, route registration, or wrapper — store.go contains only `New` and a static `Count` query (store.go:12-15), and grepping for LookupHandler/HandleFunc/Handle finds no registration or sanitizing caller anywhere. This is an exported handler method on an exported type in a library package, so the sink is added by this change and reachability is completed by whatever mounts it; absence of a caller today does not neutralize it (note `writeAccounts` is also undefined in-tree, confirming the package is mid-wiring). (downgraded from confirmed: the verdict did not state what it searched for that would refute the finding)

The sink is exactly as quoted: `lookup.go:11` takes `region` from `r.URL.Query()` and `lookup.go:13-14` interpolates it with `fmt.Sprintf` into the SQL text passed to `db.QueryContext`, with no escaping, allowlist, or type coercion — and `QueryContext` with a single string argument does no parameterisation (contrast `store.go:14`, which uses a static query, and note no `?`/`$1` placeholders or args are used anywhere). The whole repository is three files (`go.mod`, `store.go`, `lookup.go`); a repo-wide search for `LookupHandler` finds only its own definition, so no router registration, middleware, or validation wrapper exists yet — this is a sink added by the change whose exploitability is completed when the exported `http.HandlerFunc`-shaped method is mounted. Because no mount point is visible (and `writeAccounts` is not yet defined either), I cannot confirm the route is unauthenticated, only that the injection itself is unconditional once reached.
